introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER a, b and c OR d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation of your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3.0\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Answer EITHER 7 a, b and c OR 7 d, e and f.**
incertitudes: Le sujet n'imprime pas de total par question : les totaux (`points` de l'exercice) sont la somme des points imprimés bloc par bloc (Section I : 6+4+8+6+9+7 = 40 ; Section II : 20 par question, soit 100 au total).

Les schémas, diagrammes et graphes demandés à l'élève (tracé de graphe, diagramme de rayons, champ électrique ou magnétique, tension d'entrée et de sortie, schéma de montage) ne sont pas produits comme figures du corrigé : ils sont décrits dans le corrigé (axes, points clés, forme).
Question 7(a)(iii) et 7(d)(iii) : les cinq rubriques demandées (schéma légendé, procédure, données, exploitation, précautions) sont rédigées en gras ; le schéma est décrit dans le corrigé.

Question 7(b)(iii) : la distance est obtenue comme l'aire sous le graphe vitesse-temps (rectangle de 10 s puis triangle de 2 s), 220 m. Le sujet dit « brought to rest in 2 s » : le freinage est supposé à décélération constante.

Question 7(c)(ii) : les forces retenues sur la bille de plomb sont le poids, la résistance de l'air (frottement visqueux) et la poussée d'Archimède de l'air, négligeable ; à la vitesse limite la résultante est nulle. Le corrigé accepte un schéma avec seulement le poids et la résistance de l'air.

Question 7(e)(iii) : la méthode donnée pour obtenir un spectre pur (fente, lentille collimatrice, prisme au minimum de déviation, lentille de projection) est la réponse classique du programme ; le sujet ne fournit pas d'autre indication.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define acceleration and state its units. *[2 marks]*

(ii) What is the acceleration of a body moving with a constant velocity? *[1 mark]*

(iii) Describe an experiment to determine the acceleration of a moving body using the ticker tape timer. Your description should include:

- a labelled diagram of the experimental set-up.
- the procedure you will follow.
- the data you will collect
- how you will use the data to obtain the acceleration of the body
- any precaution you will take to ensure better results. *[7 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Acceleration** is the **rate of change of velocity** with time: $a = \dfrac{v - u}{t}$. Its SI unit is the **metre per second squared**, $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

(ii) **Zero.** If the velocity is constant, it does not change, so the rate of change of velocity is zero.

(iii) **Labelled diagram (described):** a runway (a long board, slightly tilted so that friction is compensated) is placed on the bench. A **trolley** stands at its upper end. A **ticker-timer** (connected to an a.c. supply of frequency $50\,\mathrm{Hz}$ through a low-voltage supply) is clamped at the upper end of the runway. A **ticker tape** is fastened to the back of the trolley and passes through the timer. A string over a pulley at the lower end carries a **hanger with a small mass** that pulls the trolley (or the trolley simply runs down the slope). A cushion (sand tray) at the end stops the trolley.

**Procedure:**

1. Fix the timer, thread the tape through it and attach it to the trolley.
2. Switch on the timer, then release the trolley from rest so that it pulls the tape through the timer.
3. Switch off, remove the tape and discard the crowded dots at the start. Starting from a clear dot, mark off every **5th dot**: since the timer makes 50 dots per second, each strip of 5 spaces lasts $5 \times 0.02 = 0.1\,\mathrm{s}$.
4. Cut the tape into strips at the marks and measure the length of each strip with a ruler.

**Data collected:** the lengths $s_1, s_2, s_3, \dots$ of the successive strips (in cm), each taken in $0.1\,\mathrm{s}$, and the time interval of each strip.

**Use of the data:** the average velocity during each strip is $v = \dfrac{s}{0.1}$. The velocity increases from one strip to the next, and the acceleration is $a = \dfrac{v_2 - v_1}{t}$, where $t = 0.1\,\mathrm{s}$ is the time between the middle of two successive strips. Better, plot $v$ against time (the time of the middle of each strip): the **gradient of the straight line is the acceleration**. Take the mean of the values.

**Precautions:** compensate for friction by tilting the runway slightly; keep the tape straight, not twisted, and free to run through the timer; make sure the carbon disc is in good condition so that the dots are clear; start measuring from a clear, well-separated dot; keep the string parallel to the runway; stop the trolley with a cushion; repeat the experiment and average the results.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A car travelling with a constant velocity of $20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ for $10\,\mathrm{s}$ is brought to rest in $2\,\mathrm{s}$ after applying the brakes.

(i) What is meant by constant velocity? *[1 mark]*

(ii) Draw a velocity-time graph for the above motion. *[3 marks]*

(iii) Calculate the distance covered by the car during the whole journey. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Constant velocity** means that the body covers **equal distances in equal intervals of time in a fixed direction**: both its speed and its direction stay the same, so its acceleration is zero.

(ii) **Velocity-time graph (to be drawn):** put time $t/\mathrm{s}$ on the x-axis (0 to 12, for example $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ for $1\,\mathrm{s}$) and velocity $v/\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ on the y-axis (0 to 20, for example $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ for $2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$). Plot the key points:

| $t/\mathrm{s}$ | 0 | 10 | 12 |
|---|---|---|---|
| $v/\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ | 20 | 20 | 0 |

The graph is a **horizontal straight line at $20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ from $t = 0$ to $t = 10\,\mathrm{s}$** (constant velocity), followed by a **straight line sloping down from $(10\,\mathrm{s},\,20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ to $(12\,\mathrm{s},\,0)$** (uniform deceleration, braking). Label both axes with units and give the graph a title.

(iii) The distance is the **area under the velocity-time graph** (a trapezium):

$s = 20 \times 10 + \tfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 2 = 200 + 20 = 220\,\mathrm{m}$

(equivalently $\tfrac{1}{2}(10 + 12)\times 20 = 220\,\mathrm{m}$).

**The car covers $220\,\mathrm{m}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A small lead ball falling from a height attains terminal velocity as it falls.

(i) Define terminal velocity. *[1 mark]*

(ii) Draw the small lead ball and show all the forces acting on it as it falls. *[3 marks]*

(i) Define refractive index. *[2 marks]*

(ii) State what happens to the speed of light when a ray of light moves from air to water. *[1 mark]*

(iii) Describe an experiment to determine the refractive index of water using the real and apparent depth method. Your description should include:

- a labelled diagram of the experimental set-up.
- the procedure you will follow.
- the data you will collect
- how you will use the data to obtain the refractive index of water
- any precaution you will take to ensure better results. *[7 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The **refractive index** $n$ of a medium is the **ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence in air (or vacuum) to the sine of the angle of refraction in the medium**: $n = \dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r}$. Equivalently, it is the ratio of the speed of light in air (vacuum) to its speed in the medium: $n = \dfrac{c}{v}$.

(ii) The speed of light **decreases** (it is smaller in water than in air); the ray bends towards the normal.

(iii) **Labelled diagram (described):** a tall transparent beaker (or glass trough) is filled with water to a measured depth. A **pin O** (the object pin) is fixed at the bottom of the beaker (for example with plasticine or a cork underneath it). A second pin, the **search pin P**, is held in a clamp on a stand above the water surface, and can be moved up and down. The observer looks vertically down through the water surface, along the vertical line through O. A metre rule stands beside the beaker.

**Procedure:**

1. Measure the **real depth** $d_r$ of the water: the distance from the bottom pin O to the surface of the water.
2. Looking from above, see the **image I** of the pin O, which appears raised, at a smaller depth.
3. Move the search pin P up or down until there is **no parallax** between P and the image I of O (they stay together when the eye is moved sideways).
4. Measure with the ruler the distance from the surface of the water to the search pin P: this is the **apparent depth** $d_a$.
5. Repeat with different depths of water (for example 4 values) and record the readings in a table.

**Data collected:** several pairs of values of the real depth $d_r$ and of the apparent depth $d_a$, in cm.

**Use of the data:** for each pair, calculate

$$
n = \frac{\text{real depth}}{\text{apparent depth}} = \frac{d_r}{d_a}
$$

and take the mean (or plot $d_r$ against $d_a$: a straight line through the origin, whose **gradient is $n$**). For water the result is about $1.33$.

**Precautions:** look **vertically** down so that the rays are close to the normal (the formula holds only for rays almost normal to the surface); remove parallax carefully; use clean, clear and still water; read the ruler at eye level and measure from the surface of the water, not from the beaker top; repeat the readings and average.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A prism can be used to produce an impure spectrum of light on a screen.

(i) What is meant by an impure spectrum of light? *[1 mark]*

(ii) Draw a ray diagram to show how the impure spectrum is formed on a screen. *[3 marks]*

(iii) Explain how a pure spectrum can be formed. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) An **impure spectrum** is a spectrum in which the **colours overlap**: they are not well separated, so the bands are not sharp and distinct.

(ii) **Ray diagram (to be drawn):** draw a triangular glass prism with a ray of white light striking one face. At the first face the ray is refracted **towards the normal**; at the second face it is refracted **away from the normal**, and the light is **dispersed** into its colours. Red is deviated least and violet most. Place a screen beyond the prism: it shows a band of colours in the order **red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet** (from the least to the most deviated), with overlapping edges. Label the white light, the normals, red and violet rays and the screen.

(iii) A **pure spectrum** is formed by using a **narrow slit** placed at the focus of a **convex collimating lens**, so that a parallel beam of white light falls on the prism (set at minimum deviation). A **second convex lens** is placed after the prism to **focus** each colour as a separate, narrow image on the screen. The colours then no longer overlap.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A convex lens is used to produce a virtual enlarged image of an object in a school lab.

(i) What is a virtual image? *[1 mark]*

(ii) Draw a ray diagram to show how the lens forms the image of the object. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A **virtual image** is an image formed by rays that only **appear to come from** it (the refracted rays diverge and do not actually meet). It **cannot be formed on a screen**.

(ii) **Ray diagram (to be drawn):** draw the principal axis, a convex lens with its two principal foci $F$ on each side, and an object (an upright arrow) placed **between the lens and the focus $F$** (closer than the focal length). Draw two rays from the top of the object:

- a ray **parallel to the principal axis**, which after the lens passes through the **focus $F$** on the other side;
- a ray **through the optical centre** of the lens, which goes straight on without bending.

The two refracted rays **diverge**, so extend them **backwards (dotted lines)**: they meet on the same side as the object, further from the lens. This gives the image: **virtual, upright and magnified**, on the same side of the lens as the object.
